prikket.explanation: "Prikket" means "polka-dotted". It is built from "en prik" (a dot). When the word after it is plural, it ends in "-e": "Hun har prikkede sokker på" (She is wearing polka-dotted socks).

primær.explanation: "Primær" means "primary". To say which reason matters most, use it before the noun: "Den primære årsag er prisen" (The primary reason is the price). To say what you mostly do, use "primært" (primarily) instead: "Vi arbejder primært hjemme" (We mostly work at home).

primært.explanation: "Primært" means "mainly". To say what a shop mostly sells, put it before the goods: "Vi sælger primært brugte bøger" (We mainly sell used books). To describe a noun, use "primær" (primary) instead: "det primære mål" (the primary goal).

privat.explanation: "Privat" means "private". To tell someone a matter is personal, say: "Det er privat" (That is private). To say who owns a place, use it before the noun: "et privat hjem" (a private home).

privatliv.explanation: "Et privatliv" means "privacy". It is built from "privat" (private) and "et liv" (a life). To say someone keeps work and home apart, say: "Hun holder sit arbejde og sit privatliv adskilt" (She keeps her work and her private life apart).

problematisk.explanation: "Problematisk" means "problematic". It is built from "et problem" (a problem). To say something causes no trouble, use "uproblematisk" (unproblematic): "Det er helt uproblematisk" (It is completely unproblematic).

problemfri.explanation: "Problemfri" means "problem-free". It is built from "et problem" (a problem) and "fri" (free). The ending "-fri" is also in "sukkerfri" (sugar-free) and "glutenfri" (gluten-free).

produktiv.explanation: "Produktiv" means "productive". To say someone was busy but got little done, say: "Jeg var travl, men ikke produktiv" (I was busy, but not productive).

professionel.explanation: "Professionel" means "professional". It ends in "-el", not "-al" as in English. To praise how well a job was done, say: "Det er et professionelt stykke arbejde" (That is a professional piece of work).

protein.explanation: "Et protein" means "a protein". When you talk about protein in food in general, leave out "et": "Æg indeholder meget protein" (Eggs contain a lot of protein).

præcis.explanation: "Præcis" means "exactly". To give an exact amount, say: "Det koster præcis hundrede kroner" (It costs exactly a hundred kroner). To give a rough amount instead, use "cirka" (about): "Det koster cirka hundrede kroner" (It costs about a hundred kroner). To agree with someone, answer: "Så vi mødes klokken otte?" "Præcis!" (So we meet at eight? Exactly!)

psykiatrisk.explanation: "Psykiatrisk" means "psychiatric". It comes from "en psykiatri" (psychiatry). To say someone is a patient of that kind, say: "Han er psykiatrisk patient" (He is a psychiatric patient). Do not mix it up with "psykisk" (mental), which is about the mind in general: "psykiske problemer" (mental problems).

psykisk.explanation: "Psykisk" means "mental". To talk about body and mind together, use its opposite "fysisk" (physical): "fysisk og psykisk sundhed" (physical and mental health).

publikum.explanation: "Et publikum" means "an audience". To say where someone sat, use "i publikum" (in the audience): "Min mor sad i publikum" (My mother sat in the audience).

pudsig.explanation: "Pudsig" means "funny", in the sense of charming and a little odd. For something that makes you laugh or is fun, use "sjov" (fun) instead: "Festen var sjov" (The party was fun).

punktlig.explanation: "Punktlig" means "punctual". To say you arrived at the agreed time once, use "til tiden" (on time) instead: "Jeg kom til tiden" (I arrived on time).

purløg.explanation: "Purløg" means "chives". The word "løg" (onion) is also in "hvidløg" (garlic) and "forårsløg" (spring onions).

pynt.explanation: "Pynt" means "decoration(s)". It is the noun for the verb "at pynte" (to decorate). To say you buy decorations in general, leave out the article: "Jeg køber pynt til julen" (I am buying decorations for Christmas).

pyt.explanation: "Pyt" means "never mind". When someone says sorry for a small accident, answer: "Undskyld, jeg spildte." "Pyt!" (Sorry, I spilled. Never mind!)

på.explanation: "På" means "on". To say where you are at a workplace, Danish uses it for "at": "Jeg er på arbejde" (I am at work). To name a language, it is used for "in": "Jeg skriver på dansk" (I write in Danish). To say you are on an island, it is used for "on": "Vi bor på Fyn" (We live on Funen).

på deltid.explanation: "På deltid" means "part-time". It is built from "del" (part) and "tid" (time). To name the job itself, say: "Hun har et deltidsjob" (She has a part-time job).

på den anden side.explanation: "På den anden side" means "on the other hand". To add a second view after the first, start the new sentence with it: "Huset er stort. På den anden side er det dyrt." (The house is big. On the other hand, it is expensive.) To say where a place is, it also means "on the other side": "Butikken ligger på den anden side af vejen" (The shop is on the other side of the road).

related.en: in return, on the other hand

på den ene side.explanation: "På den ene side" means "on one hand". To start the first of two views, say: "På den ene side vil jeg gerne rejse, men jeg har ikke penge" (On one hand I would like to travel, but I have no money). To say where something is, it also means "on one side": "Haven ligger på den ene side af huset" (The garden is on one side of the house).

related.en: in return, on the other hand

på forhånd.explanation: "På forhånd" means "in advance". To thank someone before they do something, end your request with: "Kan du sende filen? Tak på forhånd!" (Can you send the file? Thanks in advance!) To say you paid ahead of time, say: "Jeg betalte på forhånd" (I paid in advance).

på fuldtid.explanation: "På fuldtid" means "full-time". It is built from "fuld" (full) and "tid" (time). To say someone is drunk, the word "fuld" is also used: "Han er fuld" (He is drunk).

på gensyn.explanation: "På gensyn" means "see you again". It is built from "på" (on) and "et gensyn" (a seeing again). To end a visit politely, say: "Tak for i dag, på gensyn!" (Thanks for today, see you again!)

på grund af.explanation: "På grund af" means "because of". To give a reason that is a noun, say: "på grund af regnen" (because of the rain). To give a reason that has a verb in it, use "fordi" (because): "Jeg bliver hjemme, fordi det regner" (I am staying home because it is raining).

på tide.explanation: "På tide" means "time", as in "it is time to do something". To say it is time to act, say: "Det er på tide at gå hjem" (It is time to go home). To say something has waited too long, say: "Det er på tide!" (It is about time!)

på tilbud.explanation: "På tilbud" means "on sale". Literally, it is "on offer", since "et tilbud" means "an offer".

på trods af.explanation: "På trods af" means "despite". To start a sentence with the obstacle, say: "På trods af alt er hun glad" (Despite everything, she is happy).

på vej.explanation: "På vej" means "on the way". To say someone will arrive soon, say: "Gæsterne er på vej" (The guests are on the way). To name where you are going, add "til" (to): "Jeg er på vej til arbejde" (I am on my way to work).

påfaldende.explanation: "Påfaldende" means "striking". Before an adjective such as "stille" (quiet), it means "strikingly": "Han var påfaldende stille" (He was strikingly quiet).

pålidelig.explanation: "Pålidelig" means "reliable". To say you can count on a person, say: "Han er pålidelig" (He is reliable). Do not mix it up with "troværdig" (believable), which is about what people believe: "en troværdig forklaring" (a believable explanation).

pålæg.explanation: "Pålæg" means "cold cuts". It is built from "på" (on) and "at lægge" (to lay), because it is laid on bread. To name one kind, say: "Jeg vil have leverpostej som pålæg" (I want liver pâté as a topping).

påske.explanation: "Påske" means "Easter". Denmark has public holidays around it: "skærtorsdag" (Maundy Thursday), "langfredag" (Good Friday) and "anden påskedag" (Easter Monday). To say you are off work, say: "Jeg har fri i påsken" (I am off during Easter).

påskedag.explanation: "Påskedag" means "Easter Sunday". The day after is "anden påskedag" (Easter Monday), and both are public holidays in Denmark. To say you visit someone then, say: "Vi besøger mormor anden påskedag" (We visit grandma on Easter Monday).

påtrængende.explanation: "Påtrængende" means "overpowering". To say a person is too eager and will not leave you alone, it means "pushy": "Han var for påtrængende" (He was too pushy). To say a need is urgent, it means "pressing": "et påtrængende behov" (a pressing need).

pæn.explanation: "Pæn" means "nice", in the sense of good-looking or neat. To say a room is neat, say: "Det er et pænt værelse" (It is a neat room). To tell a child to behave, say: "Vær pæn!" (Be good!)

en quiz.explanation: "En quiz" means "a quiz". To say your team won it, use "at vinde" (to win): "Vi vandt quizzen" (We won the quiz).

quinoa.explanation: "Quinoa" means "quinoa". To name a salad made with it, put it in front of "salat" (salad): "en quinoasalat" (a quinoa salad).

at ramme.explanation: "At ramme" means "to hit". To say you hit what you aimed at, say: "Jeg ramte bolden" (I hit the ball). To say something hurts people, it also means "to affect": "Krisen ramte mange" (The crisis hit many people).

at ramme plet.explanation: "At ramme plet" means "to hit the mark". Literally, it is "to hit spot", since "en plet" means "a spot". To say a description was exactly right, say: "Din beskrivelse ramte plet" (Your description hit the mark).

at rapportere.explanation: "At rapportere" means "to report". It comes from "en rapport" (a report). To say what a newspaper tells, add "om" (about): "Avisen rapporterer om ulykken" (The paper reports on the accident). To say you told someone about a mistake, say: "Jeg rapporterede fejlen" (I reported the error).

at rasle.explanation: "At rasle" means "to rattle". To say keys make a noise in your pocket, say: "Nøglerne rasler i lommen" (The keys rattle in the pocket). To say dry leaves make a sound, it means "to rustle": "Tørre blade rasler i vinden" (Dry leaves rustle in the wind).

at rationalisere.explanation: "At rationalisere" means "to rationalize". To say an organization makes its work faster and cheaper, say: "Kommunen har rationaliseret administrationen" (The municipality has streamlined the administration). To say someone invents reasons for what they did, say: "Han rationaliserer sit valg" (He rationalizes his choice).

at reagere.explanation: "At reagere" means "to react". To say someone reacted fast, say: "Hun reagerede hurtigt" (She reacted quickly). To name what you react to, add "på" (to): "Han reagerer på kritik" (He reacts to criticism).

at realisere.explanation: "At realisere" means "to realize", as in making a plan come true. To say a project was carried out, say: "Vi har realiseret projektet" (We have carried out the project). To become aware of something, use "at indse" instead: "Jeg indser, at jeg tog fejl" (I realize that I was wrong).

at redde.explanation: "At redde" means "to save / rescue". To say someone was saved from danger, add "fra" (from): "De reddede ham fra at drukne" (They saved him from drowning). To save money, use "at spare" instead: "Jeg sparer penge" (I save money).

at rede håret.explanation: "At rede håret" means "to comb one's hair". To say you make the bed, the same verb "rede" is used: "at rede sengen" (to make the bed).

at rede seng.explanation: "At rede seng" means "to make the bed". To say you do it every morning, use "sengen" (the bed): "Jeg reder sengen hver morgen" (I make the bed every morning).

at redegøre for.explanation: "At redegøre for" means "to account for". The small word "for" must always follow it. To say you explain in order what happened, say: "Han redegjorde for ulykken" (He gave an account of the accident).

at redigere.explanation: "At redigere" means "to edit". It is the verb for "en redaktør" (an editor). To say you change a text, say: "Hun redigerer artiklen" (She is editing the article).

at reducere.explanation: "At reducere" means "to reduce". To say a shop has lowered the price, use "reduceret pris" (reduced price): "Alle jakker er til reduceret pris" (All jackets are at a reduced price).

at referere.explanation: "At referere" means "to refer / report". To point back to something already said, add "til" (to): "Jeg refererer til din mail" (I am referring to your email). To retell in short what someone said or wrote, use it with no "til": "Han refererede artiklen for os" (He told us what the article said).

at reflektere.explanation: "At reflektere" means "to reflect". To say you think deeply about something, add "over" (on): "Jeg reflekterer over mit valg" (I am reflecting on my choice). To say a surface sends light back, add no small word: "Sneen reflekterer lyset" (The snow reflects the light).

at regere.explanation: "At regere" means "to govern / rule". To say someone runs a shop or a company, use "at drive" (to run) instead: "Hun driver en butik" (She runs a shop).

at registrere.explanation: "At registrere" means "to register". To say an official list adds people, say: "Kommunen registrerer alle borgere" (The municipality registers all citizens). To say you notice something, it also works: "Jeg registrerede ikke, at han gik" (I did not notice that he left).

at regne.explanation: "At regne" means "to rain". To say it is raining, say: "Det regner" (It is raining). To say someone does sums, it also means "to calculate": "Han regner hurtigt" (He calculates quickly).

at regne med.explanation: "At regne med" means "to count on / expect". To say you depend on a person, say: "Jeg regner med dig" (I am counting on you). To say you expect something, say: "Vi regner med regn i morgen" (We expect rain tomorrow).

at rehabilitere.explanation: "At rehabilitere" means "to rehabilitate". The noun is "rehabilitering" (rehabilitation): "Efter operationen kom han i rehabilitering" (After the operation he went into rehabilitation). To say someone gets their good name back, use it too: "Han blev rehabiliteret efter sagen" (He was rehabilitated after the case).

at rejse.explanation: "At rejse" means "to travel". To say you are leaving, say: "Jeg rejser i morgen" (I am leaving tomorrow). The noun is "en rejse" (a trip): "Vi tog på en lang rejse" (We went on a long trip).

at rejse sig.explanation: "At rejse sig" means "to stand up / rise". The small word "sig" (oneself) must come after it and changes with the person. To say who stands up, use "mig" (myself) for "I" and "dig" (yourself) for "you": "Jeg rejser mig" (I stand up), "Du rejser dig" (You stand up).

at rekruttere.explanation: "At rekruttere" means "to recruit". It comes from "en rekrut" (a recruit). To say a company looks for staff, say: "Vi rekrutterer nye kolleger" (We are recruiting new colleagues).

at renovere.explanation: "At renovere" means "to renovate". To say you only paint a room, use "at male" (to paint) instead: "Vi maler stuen" (We are painting the living room). The noun is "en renovering" (a renovation): "Renoveringen tager to måneder" (The renovation takes two months).

at rense.explanation: "At rense" means "to clean", as in taking dirt out of something. To say you clean water, say: "Vi renser vandet" (We clean the water). To say you clean a house, use "at gøre rent" (to clean) instead: "Jeg gør rent" (I clean the house).

at reparere.explanation: "At reparere" means "to repair". To say the opposite, use "at ødelægge" (to ruin): "Han ødelagde min cykel" (He ruined my bike).

at repetere.explanation: "At repetere" means "to review", as in going over what you have studied. To say you study before a test, say: "Jeg repeterer til prøven" (I am reviewing for the test). To say something again, use "at gentage" (to repeat) instead: "Kan du gentage det?" (Can you repeat that?)

at repræsentere.explanation: "At repræsentere" means "to represent". To say you speak or act for a country, say: "Hun repræsenterer Danmark ved OL" (She represents Denmark at the Olympics). To say a symbol stands for an idea, say: "Flaget repræsenterer frihed" (The flag stands for freedom).

at reservere.explanation: "At reservere" means "to reserve". To say you book a table, Danes also use "at booke" (to book): "Jeg har booket et bord" (I have booked a table).

at respektere.explanation: "At respektere" means "to respect". The noun is "respekt" (respect), used with "for" (for): "Jeg har stor respekt for hende" (I have great respect for her).

at respondere.explanation: "At respondere" means "to respond". To say a machine gives no answer, say: "Appen responderer ikke" (The app is not responding). To say a person answers a message, use "at svare" (to answer) instead: "Hun svarede på mailen" (She answered the email).

at restaurere.explanation: "At restaurere" means "to restore". To say an old building was put back as it was, say: "Kirken er blevet restaureret" (The church has been restored). For a computer file, use "at gendanne" (to bring back) instead: "Jeg gendanner filen" (I restore the file).

at retfærdiggøre.explanation: "At retfærdiggøre" means "to justify". It is built from "retfærdig" (fair) and "at gøre" (to make). To say that nothing makes something acceptable, say: "Intet kan retfærdiggøre vold" (Nothing can justify violence).

at rette.explanation: "At rette" means "to correct / straighten". To say you fix a mistake, say: "Kan du rette fejlen i teksten?" (Can you correct the mistake in the text?) To say you make your body straight, say: "Hun rettede ryggen" (She straightened her back).

at returnere.explanation: "At returnere" means "to return an item". To say a person comes back, use "at vende tilbage" (to come back) instead: "Hun vender tilbage i morgen" (She comes back tomorrow).

at ride.explanation: "At ride" means "to ride (a horse)". To say someone rides regularly, say: "Hun rider hver weekend" (She rides every weekend). To say you ride a bike, use "at cykle" (to cycle) instead: "Jeg cykler på arbejde" (I cycle to work).

at ringe.explanation: "At ringe" means "to call", as in on the phone. To say who you call, add "til" (to) before the person: "Jeg ringer til dig i morgen" (I will call you tomorrow). To say a bell makes its sound, it means "to ring": "Klokken ringer" (The bell is ringing).

at ringe efter.explanation: "At ringe efter" means "to call for". To say you phone for someone to come, say: "Vi ringer efter en taxa" (We call a taxi). To phone a person, use "at ringe til" instead: "Jeg ringer til Anna" (I call Anna).

at ringe op.explanation: "At ringe op" means "to call", as in on the phone. To say you call someone, put the person between "ringe" and "op": "Jeg ringer dig op" (I call you). "At ringe til" means the same: "Jeg ringer til dig" (I call you).

at ringe på.explanation: "At ringe på" means "to ring the doorbell". To say someone is at the door, say: "Der ringer nogen på" (Someone is ringing the doorbell). To phone someone, use "at ringe til" instead: "Jeg ringer til dig" (I call you).

at ringe til.explanation: "At ringe til" means "to call", as in on the phone. The word "til" (to) comes right before the person: "Jeg ringer til min far" (I call my father). To say a bell makes its sound, use "at ringe" without "til": "Klokken ringer" (The bell is ringing).

at ringe tilbage.explanation: "At ringe tilbage" means "to call back". The word "tilbage" (back) is also in "at komme tilbage" (to come back) and "at give tilbage" (to give back).

at risikere.explanation: "At risikere" means "to risk". It comes from "en risiko" (a risk). To say a bad result may follow, say: "Du risikerer en bøde, hvis du parkerer her" (You risk a fine if you park here).

at riste.explanation: "At riste" means "to toast / roast". To say you toast bread, say: "Jeg rister brødet" (I toast the bread). Do not mix it up with "at ryste" (to shake): "Jeg ryster flasken" (I shake the bottle).

at rive.explanation: "At rive" means "to grate". To say you grate vegetables, say: "Jeg river gulerødderne" (I grate the carrots). To say you rake leaves, it also means "to rake": "Han river bladene sammen" (He rakes the leaves together).

at rive i stykker.explanation: "At rive i stykker" means "to tear to pieces". To say a child tears paper, say: "Barnet river papiret i stykker" (The child tears the paper to pieces). The words "i stykker" (in pieces) are also in "at skære i stykker" (to cut into pieces) and "at falde i stykker" (to fall apart).

at rive ned.explanation: "At rive ned" means "to tear down". To say a building is demolished, say: "De river det gamle hus ned" (They are tearing down the old house). To say "it" instead of the building, put "det" before "ned": "De river det ned" (They are tearing it down).

at ro.explanation: "At ro" means "to row". To say someone rows regularly, say: "Hun roer hver morgen" (She rows every morning). Do not mix it up with the noun "ro", which means "calm": "Jeg vil have lidt ro" (I want some peace and quiet).

at rode.explanation: "At rode" means "to rummage / mess up". To say you search through things for something, add "efter" (for): "Han roder efter sine briller" (He is rummaging for his glasses). To say a place was left untidy, say: "Børnene har rodet i stuen" (The children have made a mess in the living room).

at rose.explanation: "At rose" means "to praise". To say someone received praise, say: "Hun blev rost af chefen" (She was praised by the boss). Do not mix it up with "en rose" (a rose): "Hun har en rose" (She has a rose).

at rulle.explanation: "At rulle" means "to roll". To say something moves by turning over and over, say: "Bilen ruller langsomt" (The car rolls slowly). To say you roll something yourself, say: "Jeg ruller dejen" (I roll the dough).

at runde af.explanation: "At runde af" means "to round off". To say you round a number, say: "Jeg runder 4,6 af til 5" (I round 4.6 off to 5). To say you finish an event, say: "Vi rundede aftenen af med kaffe" (We rounded off the evening with coffee).

at runde ned.explanation: "At runde ned" means "to round down". To say you lower a number, say: "Hun runder 7,4 ned til 7" (She rounds 7.4 down to 7). The word "ned" (down) is also in "at skrive ned" (to write down).

at runde op.explanation: "At runde op" means "to round up". To say you raise a number, say: "Vi runder 7,6 op til 8" (We round 7.6 up to 8). To lower a number instead, use "at runde ned" (to round down): "Vi runder 7,4 ned til 7" (We round 7.4 down to 7). The word "op" (up) is also in "at tage op" (to pick up).

at rydde.explanation: "At rydde" means "to clear". To say you clear something away, say: "Han rydder sneen væk" (He clears the snow away). To say you tidy up, add "op" (up): "Børnene rydder op" (The children tidy up).

at rydde op.explanation: "At rydde op" means "to tidy up". It is built from "at rydde" (to clear) and "op" (up). To say what you tidy, add "i" (in): "Jeg rydder op i stuen" (I tidy up the living room).

at ryge.explanation: "At ryge" means "to smoke". To say you do not smoke, say: "Jeg ryger ikke" (I do not smoke). To name the smoke itself, use "røg": "Der er røg i køkkenet" (There is smoke in the kitchen).

at rykke.explanation: "At rykke" means "to move / pull". To say people shift a short way, say: "Vi rykker tættere sammen" (We move closer together). To say someone gives a quick tug, add "i" (at): "Hun rykkede i snoren" (She tugged the cord).

at rynke.explanation: "At rynke" means "to wrinkle / frown". To say paper gets small lines, say: "Papiret rynker, når det bliver vådt" (The paper wrinkles when it gets wet). To say someone frowns, use "panden" (the forehead): "Hun rynkede panden" (She frowned; literally, "She wrinkled the forehead").

at ryste.explanation: "At ryste" means "to shake". To say someone trembles, add "af" (from) and the cause: "Hun ryster af kulde" (She is shaking from the cold).
